item.title: Weak and strong discretization errors for signatures of Gaussian processes
item.description: arXiv:2611.08588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a continuous Gaussian process in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$, with independent components of roughness $H\in(\tfrac14,1)$, possibly with a linear drift, and let $X^n$ be its piecewise-linear interpolant on a mesh of width $\delta$. We study how well the truncated signature of $X^n$ approximates that of the natural lift of $X$, in mean (the weak error) and in $L^2$ (the strong error). Over a class of drivers defined by quantitative regularity conditions, the weak error at every fixed truncation level is $O(\delta^{\gamma(H)})$ with $\gamma(H)=\min(2H,4H-1)$, uniformly over the class, and for truncation levels $M\ge4$ fractional Brownian motion attains this rate. For centred drivers the weak error vanishes at levels $1$ to $3$, Gaussian or not. It first appears at level~$4$, where we compute its leading constant for independent fractional Brownian motion in $d=2$: on $(\tfrac12,1)$ it is $1/(2\sqrt3)$, independent of $H$, and on $(\tfrac14,\tfrac12)$ it is given by a $\zeta$-series. For fractional Brownian motion with drift, a level-$3$ error of the same order appears for $H\ge\tfrac12$. Below $\tfrac12$ the drift reaches the rate only at levels $\ge5$ (proved for $d\ge3$). The strong error is of exact order $\delta^{2H-1/2}$ for fractional Brownian motion with $H\in(\tfrac12,1)$, so in mean square the weak error lies a full power of $\delta$ below it. For $H\le\tfrac12$ the strong error is $O(\delta^{\vartheta})$ for every $\vartheta<2H-\tfrac12$, uniformly over the class, and the exponent $2H-\tfrac12$ cannot be improved. Finally, we construct pairs of laws in the class whose mesh data have the same law but whose expected signatures differ by order $\delta^{\gamma(H)}$. Hence no quantity computed from the mesh data has mean within $o(\delta^{\gamma(H)})$ of the expected signature uniformly over the class.
item.dc:creator: Florian Huber

item.title: Gaussian fluctuations of the moderately interacting Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto particle system around the mollified mean-field limit
item.description: arXiv:2611.08601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study, at the logarithmic mollification scale $\eta^{-2(d+1+\alpha)}\le\delta\log N$ of Chen, Daus, Holzinger and J{\"u}ngel, the fluctuation field $V^N=\sqrt N(\mu^N-u_\eta)$ of the moderately interacting multi-species particle system whose mean-field limit is the Shigesada- Kawasaki-Teramoto (SKT) cross-diffusion system. The field is centred at the solution $u_\eta$ of the mollified equation, which depends on $N$ through $\eta$. On a scale of weighted Bessel-potential spaces of negative order we prove that the laws of $(V^N,M^N)$ are tight, where $M^N$ is the martingale part. Every limit point of $M^N$ is a continuous Gaussian martingale with an explicit deterministic bracket. Every limit point of $V^N$ is a weak solution, and the mild solution, of a linear Ornstein-Uhlenbeck SPDE whose drift is the linearisation of the SKT operator at the limit $u$. The initial field and the martingale are independent, and weak solutions are unique given both, so the whole sequence converges in law, jointly with the martingale part, and the limit is unique in law among solutions of the martingale problem. The noise is $d M_i=div(\sqrt{2u_i\Theta_i}dW_i)$, with $\Theta_i=\sigma_i+\sum_jf(a_{ij}u_j)$ and $W$ a cylindrical Wiener process on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^{nd})$. The hypotheses are those of Chen, Daus, Holzinger and J{\"u}ngel, including the smallness and the nonnegativity on $\mathbb{R}$ of the nonlinearity $f$. We add radial kernels $B_{ij}$, the independence of the initial data and the Brownian motions across particles and species, a smaller $\delta$, a regularity budget on $u_0$, a strengthened smallness condition on $f$ that makes the backward system diagonally dominant in weighted spaces, and an integer Sobolev index $s$.
item.dc:creator: Florian Huber

item.title: Interacting Urn Schemes on Infinite Graphs: A Representation Approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.08611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interacting urn schemes have emerged as an important framework for studying reinforcement phenomena in interacting stochastic systems (see, e.g., \cite{launay2011interacting,launay2012generalized,WARM2014,aletti2017interacting,Synchronisation-2,kaur2023interacting,kaur2023interacting2}). Most existing results, however, are restricted to finite systems. In this article, we investigate interacting urn schemes involving infinitely many urns, where the interactions are naturally described by a directed graph. The reinforcement or drawing mechanism at each urn depends on the compositions of its in-neighboring urns. To analyze the asymptotic behavior of these systems, we develop a representation of the urn dynamics in terms of branching Markov processes evolving on a class of random forests introduced in this article. This extends the representation approach of \cite{bandyopadhyay2022new}, originally developed for single P\'{o}lya urn schemes, to interacting urn schemes on locally finite directed graphs. Using this representation, we establish almost sure convergence of the color proportions under standard conditions on the reinforcement matrix or kernel. In particular, we show that the convergence holds independently of the topology of the underlying graph, and hence our results also apply to undirected graphs, where the interactions are bidirectional. We further investigate measure-valued generalizations and other related reinforced stochastic processes, illustrating the broad applicability of the representation approach. Finally, we discuss connections with self-organized criticality.
item.dc:creator: Antar Bandyopadhyay, Deborshi Das

item.title: A tractable transition function for the Wright-Fisher diffusion with selection via gamma duality
item.description: arXiv:2611.08623v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The transition function of the Wright-Fisher diffusion with selection is a fundamental object for non-neutral evolutionary modelling and likelihood-based inference, but, unlike in the neutral case, existing representations are impractical or inefficient. Spectral approaches rely on truncation levels that grow with selection strength and the number of alleles, thus leading to rapidly increasing computational costs, while existing duality-based expansions lead to multi-type dual processes whose transition probabilities involve intractable normalising constants. In this paper we obtain a new transition-function representation for the multi-allelic Wright-Fisher diffusion with parent-independent mutation and genic selection that makes transition-law evaluation and simulation practically feasible in regimes where existing methods are costly or unavailable. The key tool is a new gamma duality, obtained by augmenting classical polynomial duality by an exponential tilting and yields a multivariate birth-death dual with fully explicit infinitesimal rates and an entrance-boundary construction. This is used to express the Wright-Fisher transition law as an explicit mixture of standard Dirichlet components, with mixing weights obtained from the dual started from its entrance boundary. We characterise the dual stationary distribution and its small-time behaviour, and develop practical and efficient sampling procedures for both transition and stationary laws, including a fast approximate stationary sampler with explicit error control. Numerical experiments illustrate substantial runtime gains over specialised methods in regimes where they apply, while our approach remains applicable for arbitrary numbers of alleles and selection coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Jaromir Sant, Paul A. Jenkins, Matteo Ruggiero

item.title: Entropic Martingale Optimal Transport with Wasserstein Relaxed Marginal Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2611.08743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Martingale optimal transport (MOT) is a fundamental framework in robust finance, yet its stability under marginal perturbation no longer holds in high dimensions $d\geq 2$. In this paper, we introduce Wasserstein-relaxed entropic martingale optimal transport (WEMOT), which combines Wasserstein relaxation of the second marginal with entropy regularization. This formulation ensures stability under perturbations of the marginals, thereby facilitating numerical implementation. We establish strong duality and dual attainment for WEMOT, which leads to efficient Sinkhorn-type algorithms. We further prove a convergence rate of WEMOT to MOT as regularization parameters vanish, and also the quantitative stability of WEMOT with respect to marginal perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Haowen Chen, Renyuan Xu, Xin Zhang

item.title: Local contraction of stochastic affine recursions of $\mathbb{R}^d$
item.description: arXiv:2611.08806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider affine stochastic recursions $X^x_{n+1}=A_{n+1}X^x_n+B_{n+1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $(B_n,A_n)$ are i.i.d. in $\operatorname{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with strongly irreducible and proximal linear part. In the critical regime where the top Lyapunov exponent vanishes, we show that the recursion is locally contractive in every direction, yielding uniqueness, up to a positive multiplicative constant, of the $\mu$-invariant non-zero Radon measure. This extends to every dimension $d\geq 2$ a result of Babillot-Bougerol-\'Elie (1997) in dimension one. The proof is based on the study of the asymptotic behaviour of the "joint process" $(X^x_n,X^y_n)$, using geometric and measure-theoretic properties of the diagonal affine action. A key ingredient is an abstract criterion for the total dissipativity of semigroup actions, which we apply to this process.
item.dc:creator: Richard Aoun, Sara Brofferio, Marc Peign\'e

item.title: Erratum to: Monotonicity of Ursell functions in the Ising model
item.description: arXiv:2611.09151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we correct an error in the proof Theorem 1 of Comm. Math. Phys. 401 (2023), 2459-2482.
item.dc:creator: Federico Camia, Jianping Jiang, Charles M. Newman

item.title: Mesoscopic eigenvalue statistics for random regular graphs: a case study
item.description: arXiv:2611.09215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study mesoscopic fluctuations of linear eigenvalue statistics for random $d$-regular graphs on $N$ vertices with fixed $d\ge 3$. Revisiting the approach developed by Dumitriu-Johnson-Pal-Paquette (2013) and Johnson (2015), we establish a mesoscopic central limit theorem in the bulk and identify its universal limiting variance. Our result applies to test functions with smooth compactly supported Fourier transforms and to a specific range of spectral scales $(\log N)^{-1}\ll\eta\ll 1$. In particular, this case study allows the mesoscopic scale to tend to zero arbitrarily slowly.
item.dc:creator: Jaehun Lee

item.title: Fluctuations of heat kernels and exit times on random graphs and application to the critical long-range percolation
item.description: arXiv:2611.09427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a graph equipped with random conductance. We give sufficient conditions for the Markov chain on $\mathcal{G}$ to exhibit large scale fluctuations in its on-diagonal heat kernel and in exit times. The conditions also imply non-tightness of the height process w.r.t. the quenched measure, while it is tight w.r.t. the annealed measure. As an application of the general theory, we prove large scale fluctuations for the simple random walk on $1$-dimensional critical long-range percolation.
item.dc:creator: Zherui Fan, Lu-Jing Huang, Takashi Kumagai

item.title: Non-asymptotic First- and Second-Order Tail Brackets for the Kostlan-Shub-Smale Field and Spherical k-Spin Complexity
item.description: arXiv:2611.09459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the Kostlan-Shub-Smale field $X$ of degree $k\ge3$ on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, we prove the two-sided bound $(1-\varepsilon(u))\,\delta_{*}(u)\le\mathbb{P}\{\sup X>u\}\le\delta_{*}(u)$ at every finite $(k,d)$, where $\delta_{*}(u)$ is the expected number of critical points above $u$, halved when $k$ is even, and $\varepsilon(u)$ is explicit for $\rho u\ge\min\{d-1,\frac32\sqrt{2(d-1)}\}$. The gap is therefore at most of order $e^{-(1+\rho^{2})u^{2}/2}$ with $\rho^{2}=k/(2(k-1))$. We also give $\delta_{*}$ itself in closed form, as a finite sum of Hermite polynomials, together with a two-term envelope that is asymptotically sharp and a single-monomial relaxation of the form $Cu^{d-2}e^{-u^{2}/2}$. As an application we bracket the annealed complexity of the spherical $k$-spin Hamiltonian at every finite $(k,d)$: the upper bound holds at every energy, a lower bound of the same form at every energy above $9/4$ times the spectral edge $\sqrt{2(d-1)}/\rho$, above twice the edge when $d\ge10$, and is consistent with the Auffinger-Ben Arous-\v{C}ern\'y complexity function as $d\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Marc Aza\"is, Federico Dalmao, Yohann De Castro

item.title: Sharp universality thresholds for random profinite groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.09477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine sharp universality thresholds for quotients of the free profinite group $\widehat F_n$ on $n$ generators by $n+u$ independent random relations, where $u$ is a fixed nonnegative integer. For products of mutually independent uniformly coset-balanced factors, convergence to the Liu--Wood measure $\mu_u$ holds when the minimum number of factors grows faster than $\log n$, which is a uniformly sharp condition. For random words of fixed length $\ell_n$, convergence holds exactly when $\ell_n$ is eventually odd and $\ell_n-\log n\to\infty$. We also prove universality for randomly ordered products of independent integer powers under the balance condition $n\alpha_{n,p}/\log n\to\infty$ at each fixed prime, recovering finite-prime cokernel laws by abelianization.
item.dc:creator: Jiwan Jung, Jungin Lee

item.title: Backward--forward interacting systems with probability-valued strategies and common noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.09487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a system of interacting agents in which a backward stochastic equation is coupled to the forward evolution of a probability-valued strategy distribution. The agents interact through their empirical state--strategy law and are exposed to a common Brownian noise. Under Lipschitz, mass-conservation, and positivity assumptions, we establish well-posedness of the finite-agent system on a sufficiently short time interval. We then identify its large-population limit as a conditional mean-field backward--forward system and prove conditional propagation of chaos. When agent characteristics take finitely many values, we obtain order $N^{-1}$ bounds for the expected squared particle--copy error and the expected squared Wasserstein distance of order one between the empirical law and the conditional limiting law. An adaptive-strategy model with replicator dynamics illustrates the theory, accompanied by a numerical comparison of the two errors.
item.dc:creator: Anderson Melchor Hernandez

item.title: The probability that a branching random walk does not hit a point
item.description: arXiv:2611.09503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the probability that a branching random walk in ${\bf Z}^d$ driven by a Galton-Watson tree conditioned to have $n$ vertices does not hit a fixed point. For $d\in\{1,2,3\}$ this probability behaves like $n^{-\alpha/4}$ in logarithmic scale, where $\alpha=4$ when $d=1$, $\alpha=2\sqrt{2}$ when $d=2$, and $\alpha=(\sqrt{17}-1)/2$ when $d=3$.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Le Gall

item.title: Singular Vortex in the Large Deviation of Empirical Current for Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process
item.description: arXiv:2611.09526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a large deviation estimate for singular current observables of the two-dimensional symmetric simple exclusion process. In particular, the observable has a non-standard large deviation scaling $N^2(\log N)^{-1}$ due to the presence of singular vortices, whereby trajectories rotating near the origin point yield an enhanced contribution to the current observable. The proof combines the heuristics of Bodineau-Derrida-Lebowitz 2008, the averaging method of Jara-Menezes 2018, and novel cancellation and multi-scale renormalization arguments developed by this paper.
item.dc:creator: Chenjiayue Qi

item.title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 4: variance under a general distribution
item.description: arXiv:2611.09592v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the variance of the reference-centered discrete total variation $d_{\mathbf p}=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}|X_{j+1}-X_j-N(p_{j+1}-p_j)|$ of $X\sim\mathrm{Mult}(N;\mathbf p)$ for fixed $n\ge3$ and fixed $\mathbf p$ with all $p_i>0$, as $N\to\infty$. We prove $\mathrm{Var}(d_{\mathbf p})=N\,v(\mathbf p)+O(1)$, where $v(\mathbf p)$, the variance of the sum of absolute values of the limiting Gaussian edge vector, is expressed through the exact multinomial edge variances and correlations and Nabeya's covariance formula for folded bivariate normal variables. Unlike in the uniform case, non-adjacent edge pairs generally contribute to $v(\mathbf p)$. The $O(1)$ remainder is controlled by a lattice Edgeworth expansion and Poisson summation; it oscillates with the lattice phases $\{N(p_{j+1}-p_j)\}$, and for $n=3,4$, where a pair of edges exhausts the bins, the summation runs over a sublattice coset. The formula reduces to the known uniform result (the classical Hoel--Kamat variance), gives a closed form when the reference law is a symmetric comb, and has a shape-independent large-bin limit for positive $C^1$ profiles. For the statistic $d_{\mathbf r}$ centered at a reference law $\mathbf r\ne\mathbf p$ the absolute values linearize: when every edge is mismatched the variance is that of a linear form in the counts up to an exponentially small error, and in mixed (triangular-array) regimes it is given to $o(N)$ by bivariate folded-normal covariances. The two-bin formulas are recorded from the companion preprints, and exact finite-$N$ reductions for $n\le4$ are used for validation.
item.dc:creator: Nikola Bani\'c, Neven Elezovi\'c

item.title: Fourier Positivity and Sharp Poincar\'e Inequalities on Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.09620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove sharp dimension-free $L^1$-Poincar\'e inequalities on Hamming cubes, a sharp quadratic $L^1$-Poincar\'e inequality on product Poisson spaces, and a sharp pseudo-Poincar\'e inequality on finite abelian Cayley graphs. These inequalities use a generalization of the Beckmann boundary introduced by Ivanisvili, Xie, and Zhang. In particular, we prove that the optimal dimension-free constant in the classical $L^1$-Poincar\'e inequality on the Hamming cube is $\sqrt{\pi/2}$, answering a question of Ivanisvili et al. Semigroup duality and explicit Malliavin weights reduce these estimates to integrals of first absolute moments of centered Bernoulli and Poisson sums. The key ingredient is a Fourier positivity principle, which shows that replacing the coefficients by their absolute values can only increase these integrals. For the underlying Bernoulli functional at subquadratic exponents, we also characterize the maximizers and determine their exact phase transitions.
item.dc:creator: Bang-Xian Han, Yuan-He Wang

item.title: Extreme-value asymptotics for smallest enclosing balls of spherically symmetric samples
item.description: arXiv:2611.09726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $R_n$ denote the radius of the smallest ball containing an i.i.d.\ sample of spherically symmetric random vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, and let $D_n$ be the sample diameter. While the asymptotic behaviour of $D_n$ is well understood, much less is known about $R_n$. Starting from a classical result of Daniels for planar Gaussian samples, we develop a point-process approach to the asymptotic behaviour of $R_n$ in the three classical extreme-value regimes. We obtain limit theorems in the Gumbel, Fr'echet and Weibull cases, with the limiting laws described by geometric functionals of Poisson point processes. In dimension two, the Gumbel limit can be identified explicitly and is universal within the corresponding max-domain of attraction. We also study the asymptotic relationship between $R_n$ and $D_n$ and the supporting configurations of the smallest enclosing ball.
item.dc:creator: Norbert Henze, Michael Klatt

item.title: Strong Convergence for Zig-Zag Products and Typical Spectra of Irregular Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.09732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the following: do existence bounds obtained by interlacing methods describe the spectra of typical random graphs? Depending on the model, we provide both positive and negative answers. We establish a Friedman-type theorem for zig-zag products of random regular graphs $G$ with a fixed vertex-transitive gadget $H$, where $G$ is sampled from independent permutations or matchings. We prove that the new spectrum converges in Hausdorff distance to that of the zig-zag product of the infinite regular tree with $H$. In particular, the new spectral radius converges to the sharp threshold established by Cohen, Cohen, and Maor. We establish the spectral limit using strong convergence and, drawing on quantitative estimates of Chen, Garza-Vargas, Tropp, and van Handel, obtain an $O(1/n)$ upper-tail bound in the permutation model. For the irregular configuration model, we show that the interlacing bound of Cohen and Maor, asymptotically $2\sqrt{\mu-1}/\mu$ for limiting average degree $\mu$, is atypical: for uniformly bounded degree sequences with a nonconstant limiting degree law of minimum $\delta\ge 2$, a random graph exceeds the interlacing bound by a positive constant with high probability. This gap is explained by the limiting spectral distribution, whose support edge is $2\sqrt{\delta-1}/\delta$. Strikingly, unlike the familiar behavior of random regular graphs, our experiments reveal second eigenvalues that remain far below this limiting edge even for the largest graphs tested. For $\delta\ge3$, we propose that the scarcity of minimum-degree trees explains this behavior; estimates for their size suggest spectral witnesses within $O\left((\log\log n)^{-2}\right)$ of the limiting edge, which is consistent with our numerical observations.
item.dc:creator: Alon Dogon, Gal Maor

item.title: Percolation on grandparent graphs of Bienaym\'e trees
item.description: arXiv:2611.09762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider Bernoulli bond percolation on the grandparent graph of a Bienaym\'e tree, obtained by adding to the tree an edge between every vertex and its grandparent. We show that the critical parameter $p_c$ is the unique solution of an explicit equation involving the generating function of the offspring distribution, and we study how $p_c$ depends on this distribution beyond its mean $m$. When $m\geq 1.569$, the offspring distribution concentrated on the (one or two) integers closest to $m$ is the unique maximiser of $p_c$ among all offspring distributions with mean $m$, and its critical parameter is $\frac1{m^2}-\frac1{m^3}+O\left(\frac1{m^4}\right)$ as $m\to\infty$; more generally, for two distributions that are comparable in the convex order, $p_c$ is larger for the smaller of the two distributions under the condition that its support bounded some explicit $N(m)$ of order $m^4$. These restrictions cannot be removed: the convex order alone does not determine the order of the critical parameters, even among distributions with support bounded by $O(m^4)$, and the extremal property fails for $m$ close to $1$. Finally, for every $m>1$, the critical parameter $p_c$ can be arbitrarily close to $0$ for general offspring distributions with mean $m$. If we only consider offspring distributions that do not charge $0$, so that the obtained tree is almost surely infinite, this remains true if and only if $m\geq 2$.
item.dc:creator: Laurent M\'enard, Delphin S\'enizergues

item.title: Limit laws for the friendship paradox in random geometric graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.09765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The friendship paradox says that, on average, the neighbours of a vertex have more neighbours than the vertex itself. We study the size of this effect, the average over all vertices of the mean degree of the neighbours minus the degree of the vertex, in the random geometric graph on the torus with the maximum-norm distance. We determine its limit law in every regime of the connection radius and quantify the approximation by non-asymptotic error bounds in the Kolmogorov distance or the total variation distance. We also give its exact mean for every $n$ and every radius below one half. For a fixed radius the limit is not Gaussian but a weighted sum of centred exponential variables; when the radius shrinks and the expected degree grows, the statistic is asymptotically Gaussian, with a Berry--Esseen bound; for bounded expected degree it is Gaussian at the classical rate; and when the expected degree tends to zero it is asymptotically Gaussian, Poisson or identically zero, depending on how fast the radius shrinks. When the expected degree is large, the proofs rest on the vanishing of the first Hoeffding projection, which makes a degenerate $U$-statistic of pairs of points the source of the fluctuations; it is analysed by Fourier series for a fixed radius and by Stein's method of exchangeable pairs for a shrinking radius. For bounded expected degree we use normal approximation for local functionals, and for vanishing expected degree the Chen--Stein method.
item.dc:creator: Mingao Yuan

item.title: Malliavin structure for conditionally independent random variables
item.description: arXiv:2611.09772v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a countable family of random variables which are conditionally independent given a latent random variable $Z$. Given $Z$, the random variables are independent. Hence the Malliavin calculus for independent random variables applies for each value of $Z$. We show that these constructions fit together. We obtain the chaos decomposition, the domains of the Malliavin operators, the Mehler formula and the carr\'e du champ operator, with conditional expectations given $Z$ in place of ordinary expectations. For normal approximation, conditioning on $Z$ and the infinite de Jong theorem of D\"obler give mixed normal approximations of degenerate U-statistics, in Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distances. Working under the unconditional probability, we obtain a de Jong type bound for U-statistics whose kernels are products. In both cases, the fluctuations of the conditional variance appear as an additional term, which cannot be removed. As an application, we consider subhypergraph counts in a random $3$-uniform hypergraph built on a latent random graph. For the count centred at its conditional mean, we obtain an explicit rate in Wasserstein distance. It reduces to the known rate for the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi hypergraph when the latent graph is complete. The count centred at its mean is a pattern count in a non-uniform hypergraph with independent edges, which gives a necessary and sufficient condition for its asymptotic normality.
item.dc:creator: Laurent Decreusefond, Christophe Vuong

item.title: The Localization Scale of the Block Anderson Model in One Dimension at Arbitrary Coupling and Volume
item.description: arXiv:2611.09776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the one-dimensional block Anderson model with independent $W\times W$ Gaussian unitary ensemble potentials and deterministic nearest-neighbor hopping, with hopping-to-disorder ratio $g$. The system consists of $L$ blocks, with total dimension $N=WL$. As $W\to\infty$, we identify the bulk localization length, up to an arbitrarily small power of $W$, with $\min\{N,\max\{W,W^2g^2\}\}$, uniformly for deterministic couplings $g\ge0$ and cycle lengths $L\ge3$. For every fixed $D>0$ and all sufficiently large $W$, the expected fraction of eigenvectors in the selected energy interval satisfying these bounds is at least $1-W^{-D}$. In polynomial volume the bounds hold simultaneously for all eigenvectors in that interval with probability at least $1-W^{-D}$. The localization length is the number of coordinates in the shortest cyclic interval containing at least half of an eigenvector's mass.
item.dc:creator: Jun Yin

item.title: Spectral Rigidity of Stochastic Operators with Heavy Tailed Perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2611.09811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we provide a new set of tools for establishing the number rigidity of point processes which are particularly well suited for the spectral processes of stochastic operators. These tools allow one to prove the number rigidity of a wide class of stochastic operators that had been previously inaccessible to the standard methods in the area, such as the variance of linear statistics, which require being able to precisely analyze correlations between individual points. We propose an alternative mechanism which uses a pathwise comparison between the growth rate of the unperturbed eigenvalues and the cumulative random noise which allows one to convert the probabilistic problem into a more tractable perturbation theory problem. This new approach allows us to prove the rigidity of previously inaccessible operators including those with heavy tailed perturbations or complex correlation structures. As a demonstration, we use these tools to prove the number rigidity of new classes of stochastic Schr\"odinger and Sturm-Liouville Operators which are resistant to analysis using the standard rigidity toolkit.
item.dc:creator: Youssef Djellouli

item.title: Global Two-Sided Estimates for Time-Fractional Diffusion Kernels on Hyperbolic Space
item.description: arXiv:2611.09890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study time-fractional diffusion on real hyperbolic space $\mathbb H^n$, $n\ge2$, with Caputo order $0<\alpha<1$. We establish global two-sided pointwise estimates for the homogeneous fundamental kernel $Z_{\mathbb H}(t,r)$ and the inhomogeneous (Duhamel) kernel $Y_{\mathbb H}(t,r)$, uniformly over all $t>0$ and positive geodesic distances $r$. By combining inverse-stable subordination with global bounds for the hyperbolic heat kernel, we distinguish a short-time local regime, a large-time interior region, and an exterior region governed by a saddle-point problem with parameter $r/t$. Both kernels have the same exterior exponential rate, while their amplitudes are related by an explicit saddle-point factor. The estimates are uniformly comparable on the interfaces between regimes, recover the Euclidean time-fractional singularities at small scales, and identify the influence of hyperbolic geometry on large-scale decay. The kernel $Z_{\mathbb H}$ also describes the one-time marginal density of hyperbolic Brownian motion under an independent inverse stable clock. This representation yields a radial limit law, moment and quantile asymptotics, and a change in the mean square displacement from order $t^\alpha$ at small times to order $t^{2\alpha}$ at large times.
item.dc:creator: Vicente Vergara

item.title: Genealogical Reinforcement in Branching Processes
item.description: arXiv:2611.08548v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Within many ecological populations, survival and reproduction exhibit a dependence on social interactions with relatives. As one example, resource excess is often shared according to genealogical proximity. When viewed as a branching system, an individual's offspring distribution acquires an effective dependence on genealogical structure. In the specific case that a large, local family structure leads to a large set of offspring, this can be viewed as a form of genealogical reinforcement. To capture this mechanism, we introduce a branching model of finite-depth genealogical dependence. Given partial observations of this reproducing population and its genealogy, we would like to reject the hypothesis of independent branching and estimate the strength of dependence. We present a statistical framework for detection and estimation, combining analytical results with simulation-based validation. We then identify our branching model with a tree-valued multitype branching process on a finite type space, providing a rigorous characterization of the expected structural reinforcement. Finally, we discuss how these tree-valued interactions can be accommodated within a broader class of stochastic processes.
item.dc:creator: Alina Kochocki

item.title: Empirical approximation of $L_p$ norms for $p\in (2, \infty)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.08896v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $p>2$ and an $N$-dimensional subspace $X\subset L_\infty(\mu)$ satisfying \[ \|f\|_\infty\le (KN)^{1/p}\|f\|_{L_p(\mu)} \quad\forall f\in X, \] we show that $m\ge C(p)KN \bigl(\varepsilon^{-p} +\varepsilon^{-2}\log_2(2N)\bigr)$ independent samples $\xi^1,\ldots,\xi^m$ with distribution $\mu$ satisfy \[ (1-\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(\mu)}^p \le\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m|f(\xi^j)|^p \le(1+\varepsilon)\|f\|_{L_p(\mu)}^p \quad\forall f\in X \] with probability at least $1-\exp(-c(p)\frac{m\varepsilon^2}{KN})$. This gives the optimal sample-size order $N\log_2 N$ for independent random sampling with fixed $K$, $p$, and $\varepsilon$. This result follows from a more general empirical moment estimate over unit balls of $p$-convex norms.
item.dc:creator: Feng Dai, Egor Kosov, Noel Murasko

item.title: On the Incompleteness of do-calculus for Universal Identifiability
item.description: arXiv:2611.08916v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the problem of causal effect identification from an arbitrary set of observational and/or interventional distributions, which we call Universal Identifiability (uID). The uID problem generalizes existing classical identifiability (ID) and general identifiability (gID) problems, which considered the identification problem from either mere observational distributions or a specific type of interventional distributions. Prior research has established graphical criteria to determine when a causal effect is identifiable in ID and gID problems. Moreover, algorithms that leverage do-calculus and basic probability manipulations have been proposed to compute these effects. Consequently, it has been shown that do-calculus is both sound and complete in these problems. Despite these well-established results, a formal definition of what it means for the do-calculus to be complete does not exist. We propose a rigorous formalization for the completeness of the do-calculus and show that the completeness results in previous work remain valid. However, for more general problems, such as uID, the rules of do-calculus are no longer complete. This is perhaps the reason why the uID problem has remained open thus far.
item.dc:creator: Yaroslav Kivva, Aliaksandra Novik, Negar Kiyavash

item.title: Group Invariance of Statistical Models and Associated Statistical Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.09087v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the group invariance of a parameterized statistical model that is closed under push-forward sample transformations given by a group action. We prove that the group action on the sample space induces an isometric action on the associated statistical manifold. Furthermore, it preserves the Fisher-Rao metric as well as the Amari-Chentsov tensor. Moreover, we establish that this isometric action is compatible with equivariant and sufficient statistics in the spirit of the Hall-Wijsman-Ghosh generalized Stein's theorem. This compatibility leads to a novel reduction of the original group-invariant model, where its Fisher information loss is explicitly quantified via conditional expectation. As an application, we apply this framework to a generalized cardioid distribution in circular data analysis, illustrating how the reduced model facilitates estimation and hypothesis testing for relative parameters.
item.dc:creator: Zhuohao Cheng

item.title: A Dirichlet form approach to the potential theory of $m$-subharmonic functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.09152v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On a bounded open subset of $\mathbb{C}^n$, we study the Dirichlet form induced by an admissible pair $(\theta,\mu)$, where $\mu$ is a positive Radon measure and $$\theta=dd^c u_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dd^c u_{m-1}\wedge(dd^c \lvert z\rvert^2)^{n-m}$$ for locally bounded $m$-subharmonic functions $u_1,\dots,u_{m-1}$. We prove that locally bounded $m$-subharmonic functions belong locally to the domains of these Dirichlet forms and are quasi-continuous with respect to the induced capacities. We establish a monotonicity property for Dirichlet forms, which motivates the introduction of $\mu$-quasi-monotone convergence of $m$-subharmonic functions. The natural embeddings into these domains are continuous with respect to this convergence. These results yield new proofs of the commutativity and continuity of complex Hessian operators. Using this framework, we characterize quasi-continuity with respect to the induced capacity for an arbitrary $m$-subharmonic function in terms of its pole set having zero measure $\mu$, or equivalently, zero induced capacity. On bounded strictly $m$-pseudoconvex domains, we prove that the Bedford--Taylor capacity for $m$-subharmonic functions and the capacities induced by the corresponding Dirichlet forms have the same null sets. We further characterize $m$-polar sets in terms of Dirichlet forms and stochastic processes, extending the corresponding characterization of pluripolar sets due to Fukushima and Okada to the $m$-subharmonic setting.
item.dc:creator: Bowoo Kang, Jaechul Lee, Zhenghao Li

item.title: Joint modelling of financial cost and carbon footprint in motor insurance claims: a BINAR(1) decision framework for circular auto parts adoption
item.description: arXiv:2611.09213v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motor insurance claims management increasingly faces a dual objective: controlling claim costs while reducing greenhouse-gas emissions associated with vehicle repair decisions. This paper proposes a bivariate, discrete-time modelling framework that links the dynamics of financial claims and repair-related carbon footprint inspired by a BINAR(1) dependence structure, allowing for temporal persistence, cross-dependence and a positive/negative correlation between the two dimensions. Using externally sourced emission factors and cost information for replacement parts, we operationalise the carbon footprint of claims under two repair pathways: new parts versus circular-economy reused parts (PIEC). We then conduct scenario analyses in which the acceptance rate of reused parts varies, and we quantify the joint implications for expected monetary outlays and CO 2 -equivalent emissions. Results show that higher PIEC acceptance can simultaneously reduce expected emissions and average claim cost, and the magnitude of the joint benefit depends on the dependence structure and persistence captured by the BINAR(1) process. The proposed framework provides a transparent, reproducible tool for insurers to evaluate repair-policy levers and to align claims operations with decarbonisation targets while retaining an explicit stochastic risk perspective.
item.dc:creator: Charles Minier (CNP, LSAF), St\'ephane Loisel (CNAM Paris), Renata Alcoforado (UFPE, ULISBOA)

item.title: The small ball problem for the Brownian sheet: sharp bounds via entropy numbers in $L_\infty$
item.description: arXiv:2611.09495v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We settle the uniform small deviation conjecture for the Brownian sheet in every dimension $d\ge2$, namely, that the logarithmic exponent is $2d-1$. Our proof proceeds through sharp entropy and Kolmogorov estimates for the associated anchored mixed Sobolev embedding in the uniform norm. Their connection to small deviations is known from the Kuelbs--Li theorem. To establish the entropy estimates, the key is a probabilistic small ball inequality for smooth tensor product atoms whose exceptional set has Gaussian measure exponentially small in the number of atoms. Its proof combines a count of dyadic rectangles with tools from probability, in particular Ehrhard's Gaussian Brunn--Minkowski inequality. This also yields sharp entropy and Kolmogorov number estimates for embeddings of periodic mixed Sobolev, Besov and Nikol'skii classes with smoothness $r>1/2$ in $L_\infty$. Finally, we extend our results to fractional and integrated Brownian sheets.
item.dc:creator: Dmitriy Bilyk, Sebastian Neumayer, Tino Ullrich

item.title: Harper's beyond square-root conjecture for random matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.09753v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a Haar unitary matrix $U_N$ of size $N$, we prove that the first absolute moment of $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Sym}^k U_N)$ tends to zero as $\min(N,k)\to\infty$. This settles the random matrix version of Harper's beyond square-root conjecture formulated by Wang and Xu, with no restriction on $k/N$. The proof is elementary and self-contained, combining exact weighted trace moments with a Gaussian change of measure. It also connects the result to the critical chaos model studied by Soundararajan and Zaman, also known as holomorphic multiplicative chaos.
item.dc:creator: William Verreault, Max Wenqiang Xu

item.title: Line crossing problem for biased monotonic random walks in the plane
item.description: arXiv:0709.3316v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A $\beta$-biased monotonic random walk in the plane moves from $(x,y)$ to $(x+1,y)$ or $(x,y+1)$ with probabilities $1/(\beta+1)$ and $\beta/(\beta+1)$. We study $\Phi_\beta(\alpha,d)$, the probability that the walk started at the origin ever visits a lattice point strictly above the line $y=\alpha x+d$, and $\Psi_\beta(\alpha,d)$, the probability that it visits a lattice point \emph{on} the line after leaving the origin. For integer slopes $\alpha=p$ we show $\Phi_\beta(p,d)=\rho^{\lfloor d\rfloor+1}$, where $\rho$ is the smallest positive root of $y^{p+1}-(\beta+1)y+\beta=0$, give the Fuss--Catalan series for $\rho$, identify $\rho$ with the extinction probability of a Galton--Watson process, and compute the exact law and mean of the first crossing point. We prove that the return probability is $\Psi_\beta(p,0)=(p+1)(1-\beta/((\beta+1)\rho))$, which equals $(p+1)/(\beta+1)$ for $\beta\ge p$. For rational slopes $\alpha=r/s$ we obtain $\Phi_\beta$ in closed form from the $s$ large roots of the kernel $\tfrac{\beta}{\beta+1}z^{r+s}-z^r+\tfrac1{\beta+1}$, and $\Psi_\beta$ as a ratio of Green's functions. For arbitrary real $\alpha$ we prove that the walk crosses every line $y=\alpha x+d$ almost surely if and only if $\beta\ge\alpha$, and we establish the two-sided bound $e^{-\theta(d+1)}\le\Phi_\beta(\alpha,d)<e^{-\theta d}$ with an explicit Lundberg exponent $\theta$. Finally, $\alpha\mapsto\Phi_\beta(\alpha,0)$ is a pure jump function: it is constant on $[0,\beta]$, continuous at every irrational point and has a jump at every rational $\alpha>\beta$.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: Commutation relations for two-sided radial SLE
item.description: arXiv:2405.07082v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the commutation relation for 2-radial SLE in the unit disc starting from two distinct boundary points. We follow the framework introduced by Dub\'{e}dat~[12]. Under an additional requirement of the interchangeability of the two curves, we classify all locally commuting 2-radial SLE$_\kappa$ for $\kappa\in (0,8)$: it is either two-sided radial SLE$_\kappa$ with spiral of constant spiraling rate or chordal SLE$_\kappa$ weighted by a power of the conformal radius of its complement. Namely, for fixed $\kappa$ and starting points, we have exactly two one-parameter families of locally commuting 2-radial SLE curves. We also discuss the semiclassical limit of the commutation relation as $\kappa \to 0$. In particular, we show that the limit for the second family with an appropriately chosen power of the conformal radius is a chord that minimizes a modified chordal Loewner energy, which is unique only when the endpoints are not antipodal.
item.dc:creator: Ellen Krusell, Yilin Wang, Hao Wu

item.title: Fluctuation Correction and Global Solutions for the Stochastic Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto System via Entropy-Based Regularization
item.description: arXiv:2501.17953v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a stochastic extension of the n-species Shigesada-Kawasaki-Teramoto (SKT) cross-diffusion system, in which a multiplicative noise term accounts for fluctuation corrections to the mean-field dynamics arising from a finite underlying population. The noise we consider is motivated by, but not rigorously derived from, the particle-system approximation of Chen, Daus, Holzinger, and J"ungel; it only partially respects the entropy (gradient-flow) structure of the deterministic system, which is the main source of the technical difficulties addressed in this paper. For the resulting system of stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs), we establish the existence of nonnegative, global, weak martingale solutions, under a detailed-balance condition on the diffusion coefficients and a smallness condition relating the noise intensity to these coefficients. This smallness condition amounts to a sufficiently large population size N (equivalently, small fluctuation strength 1/N): the existence theory thus operates in the perturbative regime around the deterministic mean-field limit, and for fixed coefficients it is always satisfiable once N is large enough.
item.dc:creator: Florian Huber

item.title: Stochastic optimal transport for the Langevin dynamics and its zero-mass limit
item.description: arXiv:2510.13238v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a stochastic optimal transport for the Langevin dynamics with positive mass and study its zero--mass limit. The new aspect of this paper is that we only fix the initial and terminal probability distributions of the positions of particles under consideration, but not those of their velocities, with Heisenberg's uncertainty principle in mind. In the zero--mass limit, we show that the minimizers of our stochastic optimal transport is tight if and only if the initial momentum (=(mass)$\times$(velocity)) of a particle converges to zero. We also prove that the limit of minimizers of our stochastic optimal transport is a minimizer of a standard stochastic optimal transport for continuous semimartingales.
item.dc:creator: Toshio Mikami

item.title: Free energy Wasserstein gradient flow and their particle counterparts: toy model, (degenerate) PL inequalities and exit times
item.description: arXiv:2510.16506v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In finite dimension, the long-time and metastable behavior of a gradient flow perturbated by a small Brownian noise is well understood. A similar situation arises when a Wasserstein gradient flow over a space of probability measure is approximated by a system of mean-field interacting particles, but classical results do not apply in these infinite-dimensional settings. We are concerned with the situation where the objective function of the optimization problem contains an entropic penalization, so that the particle system is a Langevin diffusion process. The work has two parts: the first and main one is devoted to the general study of a very simple class of models, for which the infinite-dimensional behavior is fully characterized by an autonomous diffusion process at fixed finite dimension. On the one hand, we prove the equivalence between fast convergence for the mean-field gradient flow and for the particle system in terms of functional inequalities (log-Sobolev, Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz, Talagrand and variants thereof) including the degenerate polynomial case occurring at phase transitions, and on the other hand we characterise the metastable behavior in terms of transition time between local minimiser -- establishing an Eyring-Kramers formula -- and of exit time from unstable critical points. In a second part, motivated by and building on the systematic study of the toy models, we consider the continuous Curie-Weiss model in a symmetric double-well potential, exactly at the critical temperature. We show that, although the $N$-particle Gibbs measure does not satisfy a uniform-in-$N$ standard log-Sobolev inequality (the optimal constant growing like $\sqrt{N}$), it does satisfy a more general {\L}ojasiewicz inequality uniformly in $N$, inducing uniform polynomial long-time convergence rates, propagation of chaos at stationarity and uniformly in time, and creation of chaos.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Monmarch\'e

item.title: Mixing times for the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation
item.description: arXiv:2602.00853v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We review quantitative results on the convergence to equilibrium of the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation, $p>1$, on a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with additive, possibly degenerate Wiener noise. From these results we derive upper bounds on $\varepsilon$-mixing times in different distances, depending on the initial data. We show that the Wasserstein distance to equilibrium is non-increasing in time and that, for $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$, the invariant measure has moments of all orders. For $1<p<2$ with $p>\frac{2d}{d+2}$ and possibly degenerate noise, the $\varepsilon$-mixing times in every Wasserstein distance $\mathcal{W}_r$, $r\ge1$, are $O(\varepsilon^{-\delta})$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow 0$ for every $\delta>0$. Two tables collect the convergence rates and the mixing-time bounds.
item.dc:creator: Gerardo Barrera, Jonas M. T\"olle

item.title: Regularity of the Value Function in Discounted Infinite-Time Mean Field Games
item.description: arXiv:2603.15141v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In [18], we introduced discounted infinite-time mean field games. Subsequently, in [19], we studied the connection between infinite-time mean field FBSDEs and elliptic master equations. In this paper, we further investigate the regularity of the representative player's value function $V(x,\mu)$. We first establish strong well-posedness and uniqueness in law for an extended class of infinite-time FBSDEs. In the weighted $L_r^2$ framework, we construct directional variations and obtain a bounded continuous representation of the Lions-derivative of $\partial_xV$. Under additional smoothness and quantitative stability assumptions, $L_r^p$ estimates for scalar linear FBSDEs allow us to establish the existence of higher-order derivatives of $\partial_xV$. Consequently, $\partial_xV$ is a classical solution of the elliptic master equation for the value function's derivative.
item.dc:creator: Yongsheng Song, Zeyu Yang

item.title: Truncated Signature Information for Mixed Fractional Brownian Paths
item.description: arXiv:2606.09121v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study finite expected-signature information for mixed-fBm paths with Hurst indices above $1/4$. Up to level three, the only parameter-dependent expected features are the variance transform $q_\theta$ and the time-ordered transform $R_\theta$. We prove the scale tradeoff $2K$ level-two scales versus $K$ selected level-two/three scales, together with separation and local inverse bounds.
item.dc:creator: Chunhao Cai

item.title: Equi-dependence implying independence
item.description: arXiv:2608.13559v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is shown that, if an event $A$ has the same conditional probability in each trial in an infinite sequence of Bernoulli trials, then $A$ is independent of each trial. More general results are actually established.
item.dc:creator: Iosif Pinelis

item.title: Initialization-Dependent Solution Selection by the Euler-Maruyama Scheme for a Degenerate SDE
item.description: arXiv:2610.13800v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Euler-Maruyama approximation of the degenerate stochastic differential equation $dX_t = |X_t|^\alpha\,dW_t$, $0 < \alpha < 1/2$, $X_0 = 0$, for which uniqueness in law fails. The Euler scheme started exactly from zero is trapped by the absorbing solution, whereas a nonzero initialization $x_h \to 0$ can select a different weak solution. We identify the initialization-dependent limiting regimes. The critical spatial scale is $r_h = h^{1/[2(1-\alpha)]}$, and the relevant depth parameter is $\Theta_h = h\log(1+\log^+(r_h/|x_h|))$. If $\Theta_h \to 0$, the scheme converges to the non-sticky weak solution. If $\Theta_h \to \theta \in (0,\infty)$, it converges to the solution that stays at zero for the deterministic time $\theta/|\log\alpha|$ and then evolves as the non-sticky solution. If $\Theta_h \to \infty$, the scheme converges to the absorbing solution. The proof is based on an exact scale-invariant Euler chain, a logarithmic exit-time law of large numbers, a discrete Tanaka occupation estimate, and a compact-uniform restart argument. Every finite deterministic delay can be obtained by a suitable vanishing initialization, while oscillating depth parameters yield process-level nonconvergence. Thus a vanishing initialization can survive in the limit as a macroscopic deterministic delay and thereby act as a solution selector for the Euler-Maruyama approximation.
item.dc:creator: Akihiro Tanaka

item.title: Feynman-Kac Representation and the Asymptotic Speed of the Fisher-KPP Equation with Finite-Activity Jump Noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.07868v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the asymptotic propagation speed of travelling wave solutions to the stochastic Fisher--KPP equation with multiplicative finite-activity pure jump L\'evy noise, i.e.\ a compensated Poisson random measure of finite intensity, so that the solution evolves deterministically between successive jumps and jumps multiplicatively at the event times. Our main contribution is a stochastic Feynman--Kac representation for the solution, which expresses the random field as the product of the exponential martingale of the jump noise and an expectation over the paths of an independent Brownian motion. The representation converts the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation into an expectation problem, allowing a direct analysis of the front position. Building on this representation, we derive sharp upper and lower bounds for the propagation of the front: for every speed $c>2\sqrt{1+a}$ the solution decays exponentially along the ray $x=ct$, while for every speed $c<2\sqrt{1+a}$ it does not. The two together identify the asymptotic speed in the critical-speed sense: the threshold between exponentially decaying and non-decaying fronts equals $2\sqrt{1+a}$ almost surely, an identity proved without any a priori existence of the limit $R_\delta(t)/t$. The complementary bounds $2\sqrt{\underline{\gamma}}\le c\le2\sqrt{\overline{\gamma}}$ also hold, with $\overline{\gamma},\underline{\gamma}$ explicit in $\epsilon$ and $\mu$. Under the finite-activity assumption, a stopping-time iteration yields pathwise $L^\infty$ bounds and finite-speed propagation of the level sets of the front, which underlie the existence of a travelling wave profile. The framework extends naturally to multi-species cooperative systems, and numerical simulations illustrate the informativeness of the speed bounds.
item.dc:creator: Yuhong Li, Hao Wen, Jianhua Huang

item.title: Kernel Metrics and Learning for Borel MDPs: Identifiability and Adaptive Control
item.description: arXiv:2503.11058v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider a Markov decision process with standard Borel spaces and an unknown transition kernel under the average cost criterion. We do not impose any parametrization on the set of possible kernels. To facilitate our analysis, we first develop implication relations between several topologies on kernels defined by pointwise, continuous, or uniform weak convergence; we then review robustness properties on the space of kernels, and finally we establish compactness conditions on the space of kernels. Building on this regularity analysis, we then present two data-driven identifiability results; the first one being Bayesian and the second one empirical. Our conditions for the Bayesian setting are significantly more relaxed compared with prior work which considered either finite or parametric models, though we do not obtain a rate of convergence. Our analysis is asymptotic and builds on measurability in terms of the tail $\sigma$-field of the available information. Identifiability results are then used to design near-optimal adaptive control policies which alternate between periods of exploration, where the controller acts according to a policy which is conducive to the identification of the true kernel, and periods of exploitation where the controller's information on the kernel is utilized. We will establish that such policies are near optimal. In summary, our contribution is with regard to the general standard Borel setup where there is no apriori parametric representation.
item.dc:creator: Omar Mrani-Zentar, Serdar Y\"uksel

item.title: Phase transition for conditional covariance matrices estimated by importance sampling, and implications for cross-entropy schemes in high dimension
item.description: arXiv:2511.11351v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by recent high-dimensional reliability algorithms, we study a random matrix model corresponding to the estimation by importance sampling of $\Sigma_A$, the covariance matrix of a Gaussian vector conditioned by a rare event $A$. For such models, we show that, in contrast to most random matrix models, the minimal sample size to ensure an accurate estimation of $\Sigma_A$ needs to grow superlinearly in the dimension. More precisely, if $n$ is the sample size and $d$ the dimension, we show that the estimation of $\Sigma_A$ is accurate if $n/d \gg L$ and not accurate if $n/d \ll L$ where $L$ is the maximum likelihood ratio. Moreover, we relate the asymptotic behavior of $L$ to $\lambda_1$, the smallest eigenvalue of the auxiliary covariance matrix, which suggests that $L$ (and thus the minimal sample size) will be larger for small values of $\lambda_1$. Numerical experiments confirm that this insight carries over to recent cross-entropy algorithms, with the best performing algorithms being also the ones with the largest smallest eigenvalue. Although backed up by our theoretical result, this result is surprising as these algorithms were not designed to act on the spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Jason Beh, Jerome Morio, Florian Simatos

item.title: Measuring and Decomposing Mode Separation via the Canonical Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2605.08777v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Mode separation, namely how sharply a distribution fragments into barrier-separated clusters, is a fundamental geometric property of densities, difficult to quantify in high dimensions. Modes are often the meaningful alternatives in the data, such as the conformations of a molecule or the distinct semantic types among a generative model's outputs. Mode separation is distinct from dispersion, which is what standard label-free tools capture: differential entropy rises with spread regardless of fragmentation, and PCA orders directions by variance regardless of barriers. Mutual information does capture it, but only given the latent component labels, which are usually unavailable. We measure mode separation through a single stochastic process intrinsic to the density, namely the unique reversible diffusion with $f$ as its stationary distribution and a constant scalar diffusion coefficient. From its autocovariance matrix we extract two readouts. The first, SSA (Sum of Squared Autocorrelations), is a scalar barrier-sensitive measure. The second, DA (Dominant Autocorrelation directions), gives linear projections ordered by metastability rather than variance. Under an isotropic-Gaussian null, we derive the limiting spectrum of the empirical autocovariance in closed form, generalizing the Marchenko--Pastur law. Its upper edge gives a noise floor that separates metastable directions from sampling noise. Both readouts use only samples and a score function, scaling to high dimensions through pretrained score-based generative models via Tweedie's identity. We apply our framework to three settings: (i) synthetic Gaussian mixtures, where SSA tracks mutual information; (ii) SDXL text-to-image generations, where SSA and DA capture structure that entropy and PCA miss; and (iii) molecular dynamics of alanine dipeptide, where DA recovers the known slow backbone dihedrals from static samples alone.
item.dc:creator: Shaul Tolkovsky, Ori Meidler, Or Zuk

item.title: Gibbs measures on Cayley trees and homoclinic orbits
item.description: arXiv:2610.33287v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the question of existence and multiplicity of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees with spin space $\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that, under a natural summability assumption on the interaction function, there are always at least two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying two natural symmetry conditions. Moreover, any two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying a suitable non-degeneracy assumption can be superimposed and produce infinitely many other homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures. When the interaction function $Q$ has bounded support in $\mathbb{Z}$, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a symplectomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, where $n$ is the smallest natural number such that $Q(i)=0$ for every $i>n$. For $n=1$, results from symbolic dynamics and horseshoes imply the existence of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures whose single-site marginal is concentrated near an arbitrary finite subset of $N\mathbb{Z}$, where $N$ is a sufficiently large integer. In the case of interaction functions with infinite support, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a Lagrangian correspondence on the cotangent bundle of a Banach space.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Abbondandolo, Pietro Majer

item.title: Circular flows and bisections of random regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.03763v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For every fixed odd $d\ge5$, we prove that the circular flow number of a uniformly random simple $d$-regular graph is asymptotically almost surely less than $2+4/(d-1)-\varepsilon_d$ for an explicit constant $\varepsilon_d>0$. At degree five the upper bound is $3-1/24006$. At degree seven it is $21/8$, answering a question of Li and Li. For every fixed $p\ge1$, we also obtain a strongly connected Jaeger orientation at degree $4p+1$, with outdegrees in $\{p,3p+1\}$. At large degrees we count dense bisections together with sets that violate their cut inequalities. This gives flow intervals of length $O(d^{-2})$ above the maximum-bisection lower bound of Li and Li. The finite-degree estimates, together with the large-degree transfer, also prove the conjecture of Greenhill, Isaev and Lewis that the threshold for orientations with outdegrees in $\{p,d-p\}$ exceeds the corresponding bisection threshold by at most one.
item.dc:creator: Amir Jafari
